title: Rebase and interactive rebase
summary: Rebase replays your commits on a new base, producing new commits. Interactive rebase lets you squash, reword, reorder and drop them before anyone sees them.

steps.title: Rebase replays commits
body: `main` moved on while you worked. Instead of merging, you can **rebase**: replay your commits on top of the new `main`.
```text
before:        C---D   feature, HEAD
A---B---E---F   main
git rebase main
after:                   C'---D'   feature, HEAD
A---B---E---F   main
Git takes the changes of C and D, applies them on top of F, and makes **new** commits C' and D' (new parents, so new hashes). The old C and D are abandoned (still in the reflog).
Result: a straight line, as if you started today. Merging `feature` into `main` is now a fast-forward.

steps.prompt: After `git rebase main`, why do your commits have new hashes?
options: A commit's hash covers its parent; C' has F as its parent instead of B, so it is a different commit
Rebase randomises hashes to avoid collisions
They do not; rebase keeps the hashes
steps.explain: A hash identifies the whole commit, parent included. Change the parent and every commit after it changes too. This is why rebasing **published** commits causes trouble.

steps.prompt: `main` is `A---B---E` and `feature` is `B---C---D` (messages are the letters). You run `git switch feature` then `git rebase main`. What does `git log --oneline` print? Write rewritten commits with a prime, like `C'`.
steps.explain: C and D are replayed onto E, producing C' and D' with the same messages. E, B and A are untouched shared history.

steps.title: The golden rule
body: > **Never rebase commits that other people have.**

If you rebase commits that are already on a shared branch, everyone else still has the old C and D. Their next pull mixes old and new copies of the same work: duplicate commits and confusing conflicts.
Safe:
- rebasing your **own** local commits, or your feature branch that only you push to (then `git push --force-with-lease`, module 4);
- `git pull --rebase` to put your unpushed commits on top of what you just fetched.
Unsafe: rebasing `main`, or a branch your teammates commit to.
If a rebase hits a conflict: fix the file, `git add` it, `git rebase --continue`. Or `git rebase --abort` to go back to before.

items: My 3 local commits not yet pushed
My own feature branch before opening the pull request
A release branch three people commit to
steps.explain: The test is *does anyone else have these commits?* If yes, do not rewrite them.

steps.title: Interactive rebase: edit your story
body: `git rebase -i HEAD~4` opens a **todo list** of the last 4 commits, **oldest first**. Change the verb on each line, save, and Git replays them:
```text
pick   a1b2c3d Add Coupon model
squash d4e5f6a Add coupon tests          # meld into previous, combine messages
fixup  b7c8d9e fix typo                  # meld into previous, discard this message
reword e0f1a2b Validate coupon codes     # keep the change, edit the message
drop   c3d4e5f debug logging             # remove the commit entirely
| Verb | Keeps the change | Keeps the message |
| `pick` | yes | yes |
| `reword` | yes | you edit it |
| `squash` | yes, into the previous commit | appended to the previous |
| `fixup` | yes, into the previous commit | no |
| `drop` | no | no |
You can also **reorder** lines to reorder commits. Use it to turn a messy *"wip, wip, fix"* trail into clean commits before review.

steps.prompt: Match the todo verb to its effect.
pairs: use the commit, change its message
melt into the previous commit, keep both messages
melt into the previous commit, drop this message
remove the commit and its change

steps.prompt: Your branch has these 4 commits (oldest first). You run `git rebase -i HEAD~4` and change the todo to the list below. How many commits will the branch have on top of `HEAD~4` afterwards? (A number.)
steps.explain: The fixup melts into the first pick; the drop removes the last commit. Two picks remain, so two commits. (Dropping that commit also keeps the password out of the branch, though if it was ever pushed, rotate it.)

steps.prompt: Complete the commands: start an interactive rebase over the last 3 commits; after fixing a conflict, carry on.
steps.explain: `--abort` would have returned you to the state before the rebase began. `--skip` drops the commit that conflicted.

steps.title: Fold the review fixes with --autosquash
prompt: `feature/coupons` in `~/shop` has two real commits and three review fixes recorded as `fixup!` commits:
Rewrite the branch so it has **two** commits, `Add coupon model` and `Add coupon endpoint`, each with its fixes folded in. Rebase onto `main` with `--autosquash`.
This terminal cannot open an editor for the todo list. Accept the list Git prepares by setting `GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=:` (the shell's do-nothing command) for that one command.

checks.name: two commits on top of main
checks.expectOutput:
Add coupon endpoint
Add coupon model
checks.fail: `git log --format=%s main..feature/coupons` should print the two real commits only.

checks.name: the fixes are folded into the right commits
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && git show feature/coupons~1:src/Coupon.cs | grep -q 'public string Code' && ! git cat-file -e feature/coupons~1:src/CouponApi.cs 2>/dev/null
checks.fail: `Add coupon model` should contain both of its fixes (the `Code` field) and nothing from the endpoint.

checks.name: the end result did not change
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse 'feature/coupons^{tree}')" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/tip-tree)" && test "$(git rev-parse main)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/main)"
checks.fail: The files at the branch tip should be exactly what they were before (only the history is tidied), and `main` must not move.

checks.name: no rebase is in progress
checks.fail: A rebase is still running. `git status` says what it waits for; `git rebase --abort` starts over.

hints: You are on `feature/coupons` already. `git log --oneline main..` shows the five commits.
`git rebase -i --autosquash main` moves each `fixup!` under its target and marks it `fixup`.
`GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=: git rebase -i --autosquash main` runs it without opening the todo list.
steps.explain: `git commit --fixup=<hash>` writes these `fixup!` commits for you, so review fixes go in as you work and get folded in one rebase before merging. Set `git config --global rebase.autoSquash true` to make it the default. Since Git 2.44, `--autosquash` also works without `-i`. On your own machine, leave `GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR` alone: the editor opens the todo list and you can check it before it runs.
